rights_basis.summary: FDA-authored website text is public domain unless otherwise noted. These short excerpts retain their capture date and canonical FDA link.

passages.claim: The guidance provides general recommendations on evaluating the enzyme and transporter-mediated pharmacokinetic drug-drug interaction potential for investigational drugs.
passages.excerpt: The guidance provides general recommendations on evaluating the enzyme and transporter-mediated pharmacokinetic drug-drug interaction potential for investigational drugs.

passages.claim: The guidance is intended to harmonize regional recommendations for designing, conducting, and interpreting in vitro and clinical evaluations of drug-drug interactions while developing investigational drugs.
passages.excerpt: The guidance is intended to harmonize the regional recommendations for designing, conducting, and interpreting in vitro and clinical evaluations of drug-drug interactions while developing investigational drugs.

sources.title: Clinical Pharmacology Considerations for Human Radiolabeled Mass Balance Studies

passages.claim: The guidance covers deciding whether and when to conduct a human radiolabeled mass balance study, designing the study, and reporting results.
passages.excerpt: This guidance describes the FDA’s recommendations regarding clinical pharmacology considerations for conducting human radiolabeled mass balance studies of investigational drugs, including: (1) deciding whether and when to conduct the study, (2) designing the study, and (3) reporting results.

sources.title: Safety Testing of Drug Metabolites
sources.version: Final Level 2 Revised Guidance; page updated 2020-03-05

passages.claim: The guidance addresses when and how to identify and characterize drug metabolites whose nonclinical toxicity needs to be evaluated.
passages.excerpt: This guidance provides recommendations to industry on when and how to identify and characterize drug metabolites whose nonclinical toxicity needs to be evaluated.

sources.title: Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs – Clinical Pharmacology Considerations

passages.claim: The guidance gives recommendations for food-effect studies of orally administered drug products under INDs supporting NDAs and supplements.
passages.excerpt: This guidance provides recommendations to sponsors planning to conduct food-effect (FE) studies for orally administered drug products under investigational new drug applications (INDs) to support new drug applications (NDAs) and supplements to these applications for drugs being developed under section 505 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 355).

passages.claim: The 2026 guidance revises and replaces part of the 2002 FDA food-effect bioavailability and fed bioequivalence guidance.
passages.excerpt: This guidance revises and replaces part of the 2002 FDA guidance entitled Food-Effect Bioavailability and Fed Bioequivalence Studies (December 2002).

sources.title: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function — Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosing

passages.claim: The guidance addresses studies assessing how renal impairment influences the pharmacokinetics of an investigational drug.
passages.excerpt: This guidance is intended to assist sponsors planning to conduct studies to assess the influence of renal impairment on the pharmacokinetics of an investigational drug.

sources.title: Drug-Induced Liver Injury: Premarketing Clinical Evaluation

passages.claim: The guidance addresses how laboratory measurements signaling potential drug-induced liver injury can be obtained and evaluated during drug development.
passages.excerpt: In particular, the guidance addresses how laboratory measurements that signal the potential for such druginduced liver injury (DILI) can be obtained and evaluated during drug development.
